_what: A PAID run of `news-to-social` on 2026-09-05 with the researcher's `max_iter` set to 1 and its guardrail retries to 0, so the tool-using agent exhausts its cap on its first tool call and CrewAI's `handle_max_iterations_exceeded` path runs. The subject is not the post: it is whether that path still 400s on Google.
_the_defect_this_verifies: `handle_max_iterations_exceeded` appends an ASSISTANT message and calls the LLM once more for a forced final answer. Google refuses a request whose last message is a model turn with `400 "Requests ending with a model turn are not supported."` - which failed run a9887442-ff35-4da5-8974-52fa03e81a0f three times over after nine calls had billed (benchmarks/paid-runs.md defect 2). `builder/max_iter.py` registers a global before_llm_call hook that rewrites that trailing turn as a user turn.

max_iter_check.how_exhaustion_was_measured: The hook logs at DEBUG when it rewrites a trailing model turn, and it is reached only from the max-iter call - so one NUDGE line IS one `handle_max_iterations_exceeded`. CrewAI's own 'Maximum iterations reached' printer line is gated on agent verbosity and an authored agent is not verbose, so it is absent here and is not evidence either way. The hook logs at DEBUG and uvicorn does not raise that logger, so this backend was started with logging.getLogger('brief_crew.builder.max_iter').setLevel(logging.DEBUG) and its own stdout handler; nothing else differs from the recipe in benchmarks/paid-runs.md.
